newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish sugar planters welcome 97/98 quota rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish sugar planters welcome 97/98 quota rise.

text.p: Polish sugar planters applauded on Wednesday the government's decision to increase the country's domestic sugar production quota by 130,000 tonnes in the 1997/98 growing season to 1.63 million tonnes.
"This increase was needed because Poland's sugar needs are increasing as our processing capabilities rise," said Alicja Banasik, deputy-director of the Union's central office.
On Tuesday the government also set the minimum wholesale white sugar price for the 1996/97 season (Oct/Sept) at 1.33 zlotys/kg from 1.16 zlotys/kg the previous season.
Banasik told Reuters Poland was still on the way to producing more than two million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96 after higher sowings and good weather increased sugarbeet output.
"It still depends on September's weather, which will determine the amount of sugar in beets, but we are looking at at least two million tonnes of sugar this year," she said.
Poland produced 1.573 million tonnes of sugar in 1995.

Banasik said the increase in the domestic sugar production quota to 1.63 million tonnes was also needed because as much as 80,000 tonnes of sugar was exported in the 1995/96 season via unregistered cross-border shoppers.
"Cross-border exports, especially on Poland's western border, may have drained some 80,000 tonnes of sugar destined for domestic use last season," she said.

The government on Tuesday also cut the subsidised sugar export quota for the 1997/98 season to 113,700 tonnes from 122,900 in line with international trade agreements which aim to limit subsidised exports to 104,000 tonnes by 2000. --Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
